title: YOUR BRAIN DELETED IT. ON PURPOSE.
tts_text: Last night you had a full dream. A story, emotions, people. You woke up... and it just slipped away. Not because your memory is bad. Your brain deleted it. On purpose.
subtitle: Last night you had a full dream. A story, emotions, people. You woke up and it just slipped away. Not because your memory is bad. Your brain deleted it. On purpose.
scene_role: Hook — universally relatable moment, stop the scroll
story_goal: Every single viewer has experienced this. The twist 'on purpose' is the scroll-stopper — make them need to know why.
visual_goal: A person peacefully asleep in a cozy dark bedroom. Above their head, a glowing vivid dream-bubble full of sketched adventure scenes is already dissolving at the edges into drifting pencil-dust particles — fading in real time. Middle 72% only.
image_prompt: Create a vertical 9:16 illustration on cool blue-grey textured paper in a pencil sketch style with selective color. 70% pencil sketch — soft intimate linework, gentle hatching for shadow and depth — and 30% selective color washes that show the pencil grain underneath. SAFE ZONE RULE: The top 8% of the frame must be a plain dark area with no visual elements — kept clear for YouTube navigation. The bottom 20% of the frame must fade to near-black and remain completely empty of visual elements — covered by YouTube UI. All key visual content sits within the middle 72% of the frame. In the safe zone: a cozy bedroom at night, a person lying asleep in bed seen from a slightly elevated side angle, face gently relaxed in sleep, body tucked under blankets sketched with soft pencil hatching in warm grey tones. Rising above the sleeper's head, a large glowing dream-bubble floats — inside the bubble, vivid colorful pencil-sketch scenes of a dream: a flying figure, a bright landscape, a crowd of sketched people — all in warm amber, rose, and teal color washes over pencil. But the edges of the dream-bubble are already dissolving — breaking apart into tiny drifting pencil-stroke particles and light specks that scatter upward and fade into the dark bedroom air. The dissolution is beautiful and melancholy — the dream slipping away even as the person sleeps. The bedroom background is in deep cool shadow with pencil hatching. A faint moonlight wash comes through a sketched window. The mood: peaceful but bittersweet, the dream is already leaving. Pencil grain visible throughout. No readable text. No watermark.

title: YOUR BRAIN SWITCHES TO AIRPLANE MODE.
tts_text: Think of your brain like a phone. During the day, it saves everything — photos, messages, moments. But during dreams, it switches to airplane mode. Nothing saves.
subtitle: Think of your brain like a phone. During the day it saves everything. But during dreams, it switches to airplane mode. Nothing saves.

story_goal: The phone/airplane mode analogy is the moment the viewer goes 'oh I get it now.' Make it visually split and obvious.
visual_goal: A large sketched smartphone, screen split down the middle — left half shows notifications and memories saving (glowing, active), right half shows airplane mode (grey, silent, nothing saving). Middle 72% only.

The bottom 20% of the frame must fade to near-black and remain completely empty — covered by YouTube UI. All key visual content sits within the middle 72% of the frame. In the safe zone: a large smartphone drawn in detailed pencil linework, centered and taking up most of the safe zone. The phone screen is split cleanly down the middle by a bold pencil dividing line. LEFT HALF — labeled 'DAYTIME' in simple hand-lettered pencil style at the top of the left panel: the screen glows with warm amber and teal color washes, showing sketched notification icons, a small memory camera icon, signal bars full, tiny checkmarks floating upward indicating things being saved and stored — active, alive, busy. title: THE SAVE BUTTON GOES DARK.
tts_text: Here's why. Your brain uses a chemical called noradrenaline to save memories. Like the Save button on a document. During dreams, that chemical drops to almost zero. So nothing gets saved.
subtitle: Your brain uses a chemical called noradrenaline to save memories. Like the Save button on a document. During dreams, it drops to almost zero. Nothing gets saved.
scene_role: The mechanism — the Save button analogy lands the science cleanly
story_goal: Noradrenaline is a scary word. 'The save button going dark' is not. The viewer should feel the click of understanding here.
visual_goal: A large glowing SAVE button on a screen, fizzling out and going dark — the glow dying, the button greying, chemical sparks disappearing. Simple, iconic. Middle 72% only.
image_prompt: Create a vertical 9:16 illustration on cool grey textured paper in a pencil sketch style with selective color. 70% pencil sketch — precise clean linework, hatching for the glow effect — and 30% selective color washes showing pencil grain. The bottom 20% of the frame must fade to near-black and remain completely empty — covered by YouTube UI. All key visual content sits within the middle 72% of the frame. In the safe zone: dominating the center of the frame, a large rectangular button — sketched with clean pencil linework — with the word SAVE written in bold hand-lettered pencil inside it. On the LEFT side of the composition, the button is shown ACTIVE: glowing with warm amber-gold color wash radiating outward, tiny chemical spark particles and energy dots floating around it, the pencil linework energetic and confident — the save button alive and working. Moving toward the RIGHT, the button transitions into its dying state: the glow color wash fades to cold grey, the energy particles disappear, the linework becomes thinner and less confident, the button dims and goes quiet. title: YOUR BRAIN IS HITTING DELETE WHILE YOU SLEEP.
tts_text: And it gets weirder. Scientists discovered neurons in your brain that actually switch on while you dream... just to make sure you forget. Your own brain is hitting delete while you sleep.
subtitle: Scientists discovered neurons that switch on while you dream just to make sure you forget. Your own brain is hitting delete while you sleep.

title: FORGETTING PROTECTS YOUR REALITY.
tts_text: Here's the beautiful part. It's not a glitch. If you remembered every dream as clearly as real life, your brain couldn't tell what actually happened and what you imagined. Forgetting protects your reality.
